question:
For Neurodevelopmental disorder with congenital cardiac defects and variable renal and ocular abnormalities (OMIM #621474), caused by variants in KDM2B: how can one identify which patients
have this disease from their phenotypes alone?

Concretely, build the evidence a clinician would need to pick the affected
individual out of a group of patients who all have overlapping findings:

  1. Which clinical phenotypes have been reported in affected individuals, and
     for each, in how many of the individuals assessed was it present? Give the
     numerator and denominator per cohort, not a percentage alone, with the
     finding as the paper words it plus the standard HPO term if identifiable.
  2. Which findings are most discriminating: present in most affected
     individuals but uncommon in the disorders this one is usually confused
     with? Name those disorders and say how confident the distinction is.
  3. Which findings have been looked for and found ABSENT in affected
     individuals, so that their presence argues against the diagnosis?
  4. Whether the phenotype differs by variant type, position, age or sex.
  5. Any finding one paper reports and another explicitly contradicts.

Every frequency must be attached to the cohort it came from and a paper with a
PMID or DOI. Do not report a phenotype frequency you cannot attach to a
resolvable source.
required_fields: Clinical phenotypes reported in affected individuals with numerator and denominator counts per cohort (not percentages alone)
Phenotype descriptions as worded in the original paper plus standard HPO terms where identifiable
Source citation (PMID or DOI) and cohort identification for every reported phenotype frequency
Most discriminating findings present in most affected individuals but uncommon in differential diagnoses
Names of overlapping disorders usually confused with this condition
Confidence assessment of the phenotypic distinction against confused disorders
Clinical findings systematically assessed and confirmed absent in affected individuals (findings arguing against the diagnosis)
Phenotypic differences or genotype-phenotype correlations stratified by variant type, variant position, age, or sex
Contradictory findings reported between different studies

OMIM #621474.definition: OMIM #621474 designates neurodevelopmental disorder with congenital cardiac defects and variable renal and ocular abnormalities (NEDCRO), an autosomal dominant condition caused by heterozygous variants in the KDM2B gene (particularly affecting the CxxC zinc-finger domain). It is characterized clinically by neurodevelopmental delay and intellectual disability, accompanied variably by structural ocular malformations, congenital heart defects, and renal anomalies.

source.quote: Heterozygous variants in KDM2B were recently associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder. Notably, some individuals with variants in the CxxC domain also exhibited congenital heart, kidney and/or structural eye anomalies.

KDM2B.definition: KDM2B (lysine-demethylase 2B) is a gene on chromosome 12q24 that encodes an epigenetic regulator; heterozygous pathogenic variants in KDM2B (notably including missense variants in the CxxC DNA-binding domain and loss-of-function variants) cause neurodevelopmental disorder with congenital cardiac defects and variable renal and ocular abnormalities (NEDCRO; OMIM #621474), characterized by global developmental delay, intellectual disability, subtle facial dysmorphisms, congenital heart defects, and variable renal, ocular, and systemic anomalies associated with a distinct peripheral blood DNA methylation episignature.

source.title: Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated DNA methylation signature
source.quote: Lysine-demethylase 2B (KDM2B) encodes an epigenetic regulator and mouse models suggest an important role during development. We set out to determine whether KDM2B variants are associated with NDD.

Lysine Demethylase 2B.definition: An epigenetic regulator that binds to promoter-associated CpG islands via its CxxC zinc-finger domain to protect them from DNA methylation and establish developmental transcriptional programs by recruiting non-canonical Polycomb Repressive Complex 1.1 to lineage-specific genes. Heterozygous pathogenic variants in KDM2B cause a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delay, intellectual disability, and variable congenital anomalies including cardiac, renal, and structural eye defects.

prior.text: A clinical diagnosis of KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder cannot be made definitively from phenotype alone due to nonspecific syndromic features; however, an affected individual can be prioritized among patients with developmental delay by the specific co-occurrence of congenital cardiac defects (predominantly septal or conotruncal defects) alongside ocular coloboma/structural eye anomalies and renal malformations in the absence of pathognomonic external hallmarks of classical differential diagnoses (such as distinct Kabuki facial gestalt with prominent fingertip pads, or the choanal atresia/semicircular canal hypoplasia of CHARGE syndrome).
candidate_answers: Neurodevelopmental delay/intellectual disability and speech delay are present in virtually 100% of reported individuals (estimated >90-95%), accompanied by congenital heart disease in approximately 50-70% of cases (most frequently ASD, VSD, or valve anomalies).

Ocular and renal abnormalities occur in an intermediate subset (each approximately 30-50%), presenting as strabismus, refractive errors, coloboma, or structural renal anomalies (hydronephrosis, solitary/dysplastic kidney).

The combination of developmental delay, cardiac malformations, and ocular coloboma or renal dysplasia closely mimics CHARGE syndrome and Kabuki syndrome, but the absence of choanal atresia, typical semicircular canal agenesis, and persistent fetal finger pads strongly disfavors CHARGE and Kabuki in favor of KDM2B or related chromatin-associated disorders.
Severe limb reduction defects, ectrodactyly, and coarse lysosomal-like storage features have consistently been absent, and their presence effectively excludes KDM2B-related disorder.

Truncating/loss-of-function variants (frameshift, nonsense, canonical splice site) span across KDM2B and generally lead to haploinsufficiency, while missense variants concentrated in the catalytic JmjC or zinc finger domains may show overlapping severity but require functional confirmation.

d1.question_text: What are the exact cohort sizes, author citations (PMIDs), and explicit numerators/denominators for each reported HPO finding in the definitive KDM2B clinical discovery papers?
d1.alloc_rationale: Directly extracts and tabulates exact cohort numerators, denominators, author wording, HPO terms, and resolvable PMIDs across the definitive KDM2B discovery cohorts.

d2.question_text: Does facial dysmorphism in KDM2B-related disorder exhibit a recognizable recurrent gestalt that deep-gestalt facial analysis algorithms (e.g., GestaltMatcher, Face2Gene) can separate from Kabuki or Bohring-Opitz syndromes?

d3.question_text: Are there specific missense hotspots in KDM2B that confer a more severe multi-system phenotype compared to classical loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency variants?

d4.question_text: Are any specific endocrine or skeletal anomalies reported consistently across cohorts, or are they incidental co-occurrences?

d5.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: Neurodevelopmental delay/intellectual disability and speech delay are present in virtually 100% of reported individuals (estimated >90-95%), accompanied by congenital heart disease in approximately 50-70% of cases (most frequently ASD, VSD, or valve anomalies).
d5.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: CxxC domain variants show full (>95-100%) penetrance of developmental/speech delay and high CHD prevalence (50-78%), whereas loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants demonstrate incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity.; Congenital heart defects occur in up to 78% of CxxC variant carriers and 66% (2/3) of small series, but were reported in only 25% (3/12) of 12q24.31 microdeletion cases.

d6.question_text: What are the specific penetrance rates and cardiac defect frequencies for truncating vs missense non-CxxC KDM2B variants compared to CxxC domain variants?
d6.rationale: Clarifying domain-specific genotype-phenotype correlations will resolve whether the high penetrance of neurodevelopmental delay and CHD is strictly confined to CxxC variants acting through dominant negative or altered binding mechanisms rather than simple haploinsufficiency.

d7.question_text: Does machine-learning episignature profiling reliably differentiate KDM2B CxxC-domain variants from KDM2B loss-of-function variants and other Mendelian chromatinopathies?
d7.rationale: Sub-episignatures specific to the CxxC domain have been detected; establishing their specificity relative to overlapping disorders (e.g., SETD1B, KDM6B, KMT2B) would allow definitive laboratory diagnosis when phenotypic overlap is present.

d8.question_text: What specific minor distal limb or skeletal features (e.g., brachydactyly, clinodactyly, hip dysplasia) occur at measurable frequencies in KDM2B cohorts?
d8.rationale: While severe limb reductions and ectrodactyly are absent, minor musculoskeletal findings such as hip dysplasia have been described and warrant systematic cataloging across cohorts.

d9.question_text: Can automated computer-vision facial analysis tools (e.g., GestaltMatcher, Face2Gene) reliably differentiate KDM2B CxxC-domain mild dysmorphism from overlapping chromatinopathies such as KDM6B-related disorder?
d9.rationale: Given that dysmorphism in KDM2B is mild/subtle rather than coarse, quantitative facial analysis could enhance specificity when differentiating overlapping neurodevelopmental syndromes.

d10.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: Truncating/loss-of-function variants (frameshift, nonsense, canonical splice site) span across KDM2B and generally lead to haploinsufficiency, while missense variants concentrated in the catalytic JmjC or zinc finger domains may show overlapping severity but require functional confirmation.
d10.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: The hypothesis posits that missense variants in catalytic/zinc-finger domains show 'overlapping severity' with loss-of-function variants, whereas van Oirsouw et al. (2025, 2026) report that CxxC zinc finger missense variants cause a distinctly more extensive, highly penetrant phenotype compared to the incomplete penetrance and milder/variable expressivity of haploinsufficiency and JmjC domain variants.; The hypothesis assumes a unified haploinsufficiency mechanism across variants, whereas functional data demonstrate that CxxC variants preserve protein expression but impair DNA-binding, pointing to a distinct (dominant-negative or neomorphic/altered chromatin binding) disease mechanism rather than simple haploinsufficiency.

d11.question_text: Does mutant KDM2B protein harboring CxxC missense mutations exert a dominant-negative effect on non-canonical Polycomb Repressive Complex 1.1 (PRC1.1) recruitment relative to true null/haploinsufficient alleles?
d11.rationale: CxxC variants yield a distinct DNA methylation subepisignature and a significantly more penetrant, severe syndromic presentation than truncating alleles, suggesting altered complex assembly or competitive chromatin displacement rather than simple loss of one copy.

d12.question_text: What are the molecular and clinical differences between missense variants strictly in the JmjC catalytic domain versus the CxxC zinc finger domain?
d12.rationale: van Oirsouw et al. (2026) grouped JmjC missense variants together with loss-of-function variants in showing incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity, whereas CxxC variants show high penetrance, suggesting the catalytic and DNA-binding domains dictate markedly different clinical trajectories.

d13.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of structural ocular anomalies versus isolated refractive errors across the combined global cohort of KDM2B variants?
d13.rationale: Gomes et al. highlight mild ocular manifestations like myopic astigmatism in 100% of their small series, whereas Ceroni et al. ascertain complex structural anomalies, suggesting ascertainment bias across specialized ophthalmology vs general genetics cohorts.

d14.question_text: Do CxxC domain missense variants specifically enrich for renal and ocular anomalies compared to loss-of-function or JmjC domain variants?
d14.rationale: van Oirsouw et al. observed genotype-phenotype divergence between CxxC domain variants (which confer a distinct episignature and penetrant syndromic presentation) and haploinsufficiency or non-CxxC variants which show incomplete penetrance.

d15.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: The combination of developmental delay, cardiac malformations, and ocular coloboma or renal dysplasia closely mimics CHARGE syndrome and Kabuki syndrome, but the absence of choanal atresia, typical semicircular canal agenesis, and persistent fetal finger pads strongly disfavors CHARGE and Kabuki in favor of KDM2B or related chromatin-associated disorders.
d15.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: No published KDM2B cohort has systematically assessed or reported negative findings for choanal atresia or semicircular canal agenesis (e.g., via temporal bone CT), precluding their use as validated negative diagnostic criteria.; The facial phenotype of KDM2B is described as 'subtle facial dysmorphism', lacking a pathognomonic gestalt that would enable clinicians to isolate KDM2B cases purely based on clinical inspection without DNA episignature or genomic sequencing.
d15.alloc_rationale: Resolves the clinical distinction between KDM2B and phenocopies like CHARGE and Kabuki syndromes by evaluating reported discriminating and systematically absent features.

d16.question_text: What is the systematic prevalence of temporal bone inner-ear malformations (semicircular canal dysplasia) and posterior nasal airway patency in confirmed KDM2B-CxxC variant carriers?
d16.rationale: High-resolution imaging in a multi-center KDM2B cohort would establish whether semicircular canal agenesis or choanal stenosis genuinely never occurs in KDM2B, testing its validity as a definitive negative discriminator against CHARGE syndrome.

d17.question_text: Can computational facial phenotyping and machine learning differentiate KDM2B-related dysmorphism from atypical Kabuki and CHARGE syndromes?
d17.rationale: Because KDM2B exhibits subtle facial features, 3D photogrammetry and deep gestalt analysis could detect sub-visual dysmorphic patterns distinguishing it from other chromatin-associated disorders.

d20.question_text: What are the exact patient-by-patient clinical numerators and denominators for cardiac, ocular, renal, and neurological features in the original clinical delineation paper by the episignature consortium referenced in Ceroni et al. and Kato et al.?
d20.rationale: Accessing the full-text tables of the primary delineation paper ('Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated DNA episignature') will yield the exact counts and HPO term mappings required for definitive prevalence calculations.
d20.alloc_rationale: Directly targets exact cohort numerators, denominators, and verbatim clinical phenotypes with HPO terms from the primary clinical delineation paper.

d21.question_text: Does the phenotypic spectrum of Commander-complex-associated Ritscher-Schinzel syndrome overlap with KDM2B-associated neurodevelopmental disorder in specific renal (proteinuria vs cystic dysplasia) and cardiac phenotypes?
d21.rationale: Recent literature (Kato et al. 2024/2025) directly compares RSS malformations (cardiac defects, cerebellar dysplasia, and kidney dysfunction) to KDM2B-related disorders, suggesting possible convergent pathways in organogenesis.

d22.question_text: In comprehensive cohort studies of KDM2B, what proportion of patients have undergone targeted temporal bone CT and flexible nasopharyngoscopy to definitively confirm or refute the true absence of semicircular canal hypoplasia and choanal stenosis?
d22.rationale: Assessing how frequently these CHARGE-defining examinations were actually performed with negative results will clarify whether they serve as true exclusionary criteria or reflect an ascertainment gap.

d23.question_text: Does computer-assisted facial gestalt analysis (e.g., GestaltMatcher or DeepGestalt) achieve statistically significant discrimination between KDM2B-related disorder, KMT2D-related Kabuki syndrome, and CHD7-related CHARGE syndrome?
d23.rationale: Quantifying the objective divergence of 2D/3D facial feature vectors will verify whether subtle facial dysmorphisms in KDM2B contain discriminatory information or if episignature analysis remains indispensable.

d24.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: In the definitive clinical discovery cohort establishing OMIM #621474, neurodevelopmental impairment/intellectual disability is an obligate feature (100% numerator/denominator in patients evaluated after 2 years of age), whereas congenital heart defects have a frequency of 50-70% and structural renal anomalies occur in under 40% of cases.
d24.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: CHD penetrance depends heavily on variant domain: while CHD occurs in 60% of pLOF variants (3/5), it reaches 77.8% (14/18) to 78% in CxxC-domain variants (exceeding the proposed 50-70% range), and drops to 0% in JmjC variants.; van Oirsouw et al. (2026) report incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity among pLOF and JmjC variants, contradicting the assertion that neurodevelopmental impairment is an obligate 100% penetrant feature across all individuals.
d24.alloc_rationale: Resolves key contradictions in neurodevelopmental, cardiac, and renal penetrance stratified across CxxC, JmjC, and truncating variant classes.

d25.question_text: What is the true penetrance of non-syndromic versus syndromic neurodevelopmental impairment among unselected adult carriers of KDM2B loss-of-function variants in population biobanks?
d25.rationale: Clinical discovery cohorts suffer from ascertainment bias towards severe presentations. Van Oirsouw et al. (2026) identified incomplete penetrance for pLOF variants, which needs systematic quantification in unselected population databases (e.g., UK Biobank, All of Us).

d26.question_text: Does the specific CxxC domain DNA-binding disruption cause structural cardiac and urogenital defects via a dominant-negative or gain-of-function mechanism compared to haploinsufficiency?
d26.rationale: CHD and other extra-CNS structural malformations are heavily concentrated in CxxC domain variants (up to 78%) compared to JmjC and haploinsufficient alleles, suggesting distinct molecular pathology that could delineate subtype-specific diagnostic criteria.

d27.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: A specific peripheral blood DNA methylation episignature distinguishes KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder from clinically overlapping chromatin and recyclinopathy disorders (such as CHARGE, Kabuki, and Ritscher-Schinzel syndromes) with >95% sensitivity and specificity.
d27.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: KDM2B exhibits divergence into two distinct sub-episignatures (loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency vs CxxC domain missense variants), contradicting the assumption of a single uniform episignature classifier.; Partial episignature matches have been observed between KDM2B and other chromatin-modifying neurodevelopmental disorder signatures, demonstrating cross-classification ambiguity.; Standard episignature classifiers display reduced sensitivity for hypomorphic variants and somatic mosaicism, challenging strict >95% clinical sensitivity assertions across broader patient cohorts.

d28.question_text: Does an ensemble classifier combining the KDM2B haploinsufficiency subsignature and the CxxC domain-specific subsignature improve diagnostic sensitivity for moderate-effect VUS?
d28.rationale: Because KDM2B variants generate bifurcated subsignatures with distinct biological mechanisms (loss-of-function vs dominant/altered DNA binding), dual-model classification could prevent misclassification of CxxC missense variants.

d29.question_text: What is the exact pairwise classification specificity between KDM2B CxxC subsignatures and CHD7 (CHARGE syndrome) / KMT2D (Kabuki syndrome) peripheral blood episignatures?
d29.rationale: Direct receiver operating characteristic (ROC) benchmark comparisons on shared clinical cohorts presenting with heart, eye, and renal malformations are necessary to prove the >95% specificity claim over phenocopies.

d30.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: Individuals carrying heterozygous pathogenic variants in the CxxC zinc-finger domain of KDM2B exhibit a significantly higher penetrance of structural ocular malformations (microphthalmia, coloboma) and multi-organ anomalies mimicking CHARGE/Kabuki syndrome than individuals with non-CxxC loss-of-function variants.
d30.rationale: deep test attempt 2 left this contested: While Ceroni et al. emphasize CxxC zinc-finger missense variants as driving developmental eye malformations, general loss-of-function models (Iwagawa et al., 2023; Ceroni et al., 2026) produce identical structural ocular phenotypes (coloboma in ~40% of full-length null mouse embryos, and microphthalmia upon retinal knockout).; Human clinical data from van Jaarsveld et al. (2022) demonstrate that both loss-of-function and CxxC domain variants display multi-organ congenital anomalies (ocular, cardiac, urogenital), with no statistically significant increase in penetrance formally demonstrated for CxxC missense variants over loss-of-function alleles in current human cohorts.

d31.question_text: Does an unselected, international registry of KDM2B-variant individuals reveal a statistically significant difference in ocular structural anomaly penetrance between CxxC missense variants and truncating/frameshift LoF variants?
d31.rationale: Current cohorts are biased by targeted ascertainment (e.g., screening 706 eye disorder families). Comparing unselected or neurodevelopmentally ascertain cohorts is required to accurately establish genotype-phenotype penetrance.

d32.question_text: Do CxxC missense variants act via a dominant-negative mechanism on PRC1.1 assembly at unmethylated CpG islands compared to true haploinsufficiency?
d32.rationale: Determining whether CxxC mutations preserve interaction with BCOR/PCGF1 while disrupting DNA binding could explain subepisignature divergence and potential tissue-specific phenotypic severity.

d33.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: A clinical diagnosis of KDM2B-related disorder cannot be established solely on facial dysmorphology or non-molecular criteria because KDM2B lacks a discrete facial gestalt, requiring genome-wide DNA methylation episignature analysis to resolve classification from Kabuki and CHARGE syndromes.
d33.rationale: deep test attempt 2 left this contested: van Oirsouw et al. (2026) report that individuals with KDM2B CxxC-domain variants display distinct facial features that can be objectively separated and identified using GestaltMatcher, directly conflicting with the hypothesis premise that KDM2B completely lacks a discrete facial gestalt.; While peripheral blood DNA methylation episignatures assist in resolving variants of uncertain significance and subclassification, clinical diagnosis can be achieved through molecular sequencing (exome/genome sequencing) rather than requiring episignature analysis in all presentations.

d34.question_text: How effectively can computer vision algorithms like GestaltMatcher differentiate KDM2B-CxxC facial phenotypes from Kabuki (KMT2D/KDM6A) and CHARGE (CHD7) syndrome cohorts?
d34.rationale: The hypothesis asserts that episignature profiling is strictly required to resolve KDM2B from Kabuki and CHARGE due to phenotypic and facial overlap; testing facial recognition models directly between these cohorts will assess non-molecular discriminatory power.

d35.question_text: What is the sensitivity and false-negative rate of the KDM2B blood episignature among non-CxxC missense variants and loss-of-function variants with incomplete penetrance?
d35.rationale: van Oirsouw et al. noted that some non-CxxC or loss-of-function variants tested negative for the general KDM2B episignature, indicating that episignatures alone may fail to capture the full spectrum of KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder.

d36.question_text: What is the true prevalence of semicircular canal hypoplasia or inner ear malformations on high-resolution temporal bone CT in molecularly confirmed KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder?
d36.rationale: Temporal bone imaging has not been systematically conducted or reported in KDM2B cohorts; establishing whether semicircular canal hypoplasia occurs in KDM2B patients will determine whether it is a truly specific discriminator for CHARGE syndrome.

d37.question_text: Can peripheral blood DNA methylation episignatures definitively separate KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder from CHD7-related CHARGE syndrome in patients with ambiguous clinical presentations?
d37.rationale: Both KDM2B and CHD7 function in epigenetic regulation and chromatin remodeling; validating distinct, non-overlapping genome-wide DNA methylation signatures could offer a robust diagnostic classifier when clinical features overlap.

d38.question_text: Re-investigate (refuted): Missense variants clustered within the CxxC zinc finger domain of KDM2B (amino acids ~600-650) demonstrate significantly higher penetrance of severe structural eye anomalies (coloboma, microphthalmia, anophthalmia; >75%) compared to truncating loss-of-function variants across KDM2B (<30%).
d38.rationale: deep test refuted it: The hypothesis posits that missense variants in the CxxC zinc finger domain of KDM2B have >75% penetrance for severe structural eye anomalies (coloboma, microphthalmia, anophthalmia). However, clinical series of patients with CxxC domain variants explicitly contradict this high penetrance rate. Specifically, Gomes et al. (2026) report three consecutive individuals with KDM2B CxxC domain variants who all exhibited non-structural refractive errors (myopic astigmatism) rather than severe structural anomalies (0/3, 0%). Furthermore, while Ceroni et al. (2026) identified two cases with structural eye defects, this cohort was ascertained by intentionally screening 706 families already presenting with developmental eye disorders, introducing strong ascertainment bias. In broader cohorts of CxxC domain variants (van Oirsouw et al., 2025; Gomes et al., 2026), ophthalmological anomalies are common, but severe structural malformations do not approach >75% penetrance.

d39.question_text: What is the true unbiased penetrance of structural ocular anomalies versus refractive errors across all known individuals with KDM2B CxxC missense variants?
d39.rationale: Current cohorts differ drastically by ascertainment criteria (ophthalmic vs neurodevelopmental clinics), obscuring true penetrance.

d40.question_text: Do specific residues within the CxxC domain (e.g., zinc-coordinating cysteines vs basic DNA-contact residues) differentially affect ocular organogenesis pathways?
d40.rationale: Differences in residual DNA binding or PRC1.1 recruitment between missense variants may explain why some patients develop coloboma/microphthalmia while others develop only refractive errors.

d41.question_text: What are the exact sub-categorized cardiac anatomical subtypes (e.g., ASD vs VSD vs valve stenosis vs conotruncal anomalies) in the 47 pathogenic cases from van Oirsouw et al. (2026) to differentiate KDM2B from CHD7-associated heart malformations?
d41.rationale: CHARGE syndrome characteristically exhibits conotruncal defects and tetralogy of Fallot, whereas KDM2B reports frequently cite septal defects; extracting the exact sub-phenotype numbers will establish clear discriminating criteria.

d42.question_text: What is the exact incidence of anterior versus posterior segment structural eye anomalies (coloboma/microphthalmia vs refractive error/strabismus) in the CxxC vs non-CxxC cohorts across van Jaarsveld (2023), Ceroni (2026), and van Oirsouw (2026)?
d42.rationale: Clarifying whether coloboma is exclusive to the CxxC zinc finger domain will resolve whether ophthalmologic examination can pinpoint the variant domain before molecular sequencing.

d43.question_text: What specific congenital heart defect subtypes (e.g., ASD, VSD, tetralogy of Fallot, or valve malformations) distinguish KDM2B CxxC-domain variants from 12q24.31 microdeletions and other chromatin-associated NDDs?
d43.rationale: Identifying specific lesion patterns will refine bedside differentiation and clarify whether CxxC variants drive distinct cardiac morphogenetic defects compared to broad chromosomal haploinsufficiency.

d44.question_text: What proportion of asymptomatic or mildly affected parents transmit pathogenic KDM2B pLOF or JmjC variants, and what modifier mechanisms account for the incomplete penetrance?
d44.rationale: Clarifying familial inheritance rates and incomplete penetrance is essential for accurate genetic counseling and variant reclassification under ACMG/AMP criteria.

d45.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of structural cardiac defects in pure non-CxxC KDM2B loss-of-function variants versus CxxC missense variants across all currently published cohorts?
d45.rationale: Clarifying the exact subgroup-specific organ penetrance will establish whether cardiac screening protocols can be tiered based on variant location and class.

d46.question_text: Do non-CxxC truncating variants alter Polycomb Repressive Complex 1.1 assembly differently than DNA-binding defective CxxC point mutations during cardiogenesis?
d46.rationale: Differences in dominant-negative or neomorphic mechanism versus strict haploinsufficiency may explain why congenital heart defects are strongly tied to CxxC domain mutations.

d47.question_text: Does dominant-negative interference with non-canonical Polycomb repressive complex 1 (PRC1.1) assembly specifically drive the 100% penetrant CxxC phenotype compared to simple haploinsufficiency?
d47.rationale: Differences in penetrance between CxxC domain missense variants and pLOF/truncating variants suggest a dominant-negative or gain-of-function mechanism targeting CpG island chromatin recruitment.

d48.question_text: What genetic modifiers or epistatic loci determine neurodevelopmental penetrance in asymptomatic pLOF KDM2B carriers?
d48.rationale: Approximately 50% of individuals carrying KDM2B pLOF variants develop DD/ID, indicating the existence of protective genomic or epigenetic buffering mechanisms.

d49.question_text: Does dominant-negative interference or gain-of-function by CxxC-mutant KDM2B account for the heightened cardiac penetrance compared to pure haploinsufficiency?
d49.rationale: van Oirsouw et al. (2025) demonstrated that mutant KDM2B proteins with CxxC alterations are stably expressed in vitro but show impaired DNA binding and distinct subepisignatures, suggesting a non-haploinsufficient mechanism that may dysregulate cardiogenic transcriptional programs more severely than loss-of-function alleles.

d50.question_text: What modifier genes within the 12q24.31 contiguous deletion locus or compensatory transcriptional pathways explain the lower penetrance of congenital heart defects in deletion carriers compared to point mutations?
d50.rationale: Contiguous deletions typically result in more severe phenotypes, but in KDM2B/12q24.31, CHD is reported in only 25% of microdeletions versus ~78% in CxxC missense variants, suggesting deletion may not trigger the specific aberrant chromatin-binding dynamics of CxxC point mutants.

d51.question_text: Resolve the conflict over: Renal structural anomalies (specifically unilateral renal agenesis or solitary dysplastic kidney) occur in exactly 33% (1/3) to under 45% of patients with CxxC domain variants, indicating that structural nephrourological abnormalities are an ancillary rather than an obligate feature of OMIM #621474.
d51.rationale: deep test attempt 1 left this contested: The hypothesis posits a prevalence of exactly 33% to under 45% for structural renal anomalies in KDM2B CxxC variants. patterns.pattern: Domain-specific functional disruption dictates multisystem syndromic penetrance versus isolated neurodevelopmental delay
patterns.abstraction: Allelic heterogeneity wherein missense alterations within specialized structural binding motifs trigger distinct, highly penetrant syndromic malformations, while general truncating loss-of-function variants across the gene produce milder, variable, or isolated neurocognitive phenotypes.
patterns.instance: In KDM2B, missense variants clustered within the CxxC zinc finger domain produce congenital heart defects in 74% to 78% (14/19) of cases with complete neurodevelopmental penetrance, whereas non-CxxC premature loss-of-function variants (pLOF) yield CHD in 60% (3/5), contiguous 12q24.31 microdeletions yield CHD in 25% (3/12), and JmjC domain variants display incomplete penetrance (<50% multisystem triad).
